To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

unit level transformational leaders' idealised influence and their inspirational motivation, when taken together, have a positive indirect effect on work unit innovation performance through unit knowledge sharing climate (mediator 1) and internal to unit employee knowledge sharing (mediator 2).

unit leaders who are transformational in terms of their idealized influence and inspirational motivation behaviours create an environment where unit members are more likely to share knowledge with each other and this in turn is associated with unit innovation performance.

unit level transformational leaders’ behaviours, particularly their idealized influence and their inspirational motivation, have positive effects on work unit innovation performance, and that these positive effects are mediated by unit knowledge sharing climate, which in turn is mediated by internal to unit knowledge transfer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

transformational leadership is an important antecedent to work unit innovation and this relationship is explained by the double mediation mechanism of internal knowledge sharing and unit knowledge sharing climate.

the more leaders are perceived to behave with idealised influence and inspire others, the more employees will share knowledge within the work unit and the more likely the work unit will be innovative.

unit level transformational leaders who display idealised influence and who inspire their followers to be innovative, are more likely to have employees who share more knowledge with their colleagues, which in turn leads to more innovation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the unit level TFL behaviours of idealised influence and inspiration are important for the innovation performance of work units and that these TFL behaviours have their effects through a double mediation process involving unit knowledge sharing and internal to unit sharing.

TFL behaviours are important in generating knowledge sharing and innovation in organisations, and that these behaviours need to be considered in tandem with other contextual variables in order to understand the innovation performance of work units in contemporary organisations.

unit leaders who are transformational in their behaviours and who engage in knowledge sharing with employees will be able to create the conditions for employees to share knowledge with one another, which in turn will lead to innovation.
